sources.title: Fastned: EV brand overview pages with per-vehicle charge curves (Nissan, Hyundai, Kia)
sources.notes: Each vehicle section embeds a per-percent kW series (JSON in the chart element); read from the public page HTML (Hyundai https://www.fastnedcharging.com/en/brands-overview/hyundai, Kia .../kia). Fastned: the chart shows charging behaviour with the battery in optimal conditions (around 30 °C). The Fastned terms page (customer charging terms) was checked and has no clause on reuse of the curve data; EV Database also credits data made available by Fastned. Not independently verified method.

curves.notes: Fastned vehicle page chart data (the page embeds a per-percent kW series); Fastned says the curve shows the car on its network with the battery in optimal conditions (around 30 °C), and a colder or warmer battery can charge much slower. Sampled every 5 % plus the first, last and peak points. Fastned does not state the session count, ambient temperature or preconditioning. Fastned page covers the 24 kWh Leaf 2011-2018 (air-cooled, CHAdeMO 50 kW). Starts at 1 % and runs to the end of the series.

Fastned vehicle page chart data (the page embeds a per-percent kW series); Fastned says the curve shows the car on its network with the battery in optimal conditions (around 30 °C), and a colder or warmer battery can charge much slower. Sampled every 5 % plus the first, last and peak points. Fastned does not state the session count, ambient temperature or preconditioning. Fastned page covers the 40 kWh Leaf 2018-2024; applied to 2025 as no change to the pack or charging hardware is known. Second source: EverTV (evercars.com) 2018-2025 Leaf S CHAdeMO test (mild weather, no preconditioning) reports about 45 kW at the start (under 10 %) with a 47 kW peak near 16 %, 45 kW held to the mid-50s, 35 kW at 65 % and 25 kW at 80 %, 10-80 % in 37 min 38 s; this agrees with the Fastned shape (45.6 kW at 60 %, 36.5 at 65 %, 26 at 80 %). Leaf throttles hard when the pack is hot: repeated fast charges are slower (rapidgate).

Fastned vehicle page chart data (the page embeds a per-percent kW series); Fastned says the curve shows the car on its network with the battery in optimal conditions (around 30 °C), and a colder or warmer battery can charge much slower. Sampled every 5 % plus the first, last and peak points. Fastned does not state the session count, ambient temperature or preconditioning. Fastned page for the 87 kWh ARIYA (2022+). The series starts at 7 % with 144-149 kW for 7-15 % before stepping down to 129-131 kW at 16 %; the 7-15 % section is left out here because it is above the 130 kW Nissan peak (the linter allows 5 % over) and nothing else supports it. Recorded series therefore begins at 16 %. Cross-check: State Of Charge (Tom Moloughney) 2025 ARIYA Platinum+ e-4ORCE test on an EVgo 325 kW charger via evchargingstations.com reports a 130 kW peak held from about 3 % to 56 %, 10-80 % in 31.5 min (110 kW average), consistent in shape with the 130 kW plateau, ~95 kW at 60 % and 56 kW at 80 % here (Fastned 10-80 % average is lower); that source gives no point table.

Fastned page for the 64 kWh Kona Electric 2018-2022 (Fastned lists Kona and e-Niro 64 kWh with the identical series, same pack and hardware); applied to 2023 Kona Electric on the same powertrain. Step-like fall (76 kW at 40 %, 71 at 50 %, 57 at 60 %, 37 at 75 %, 25 at 80 %) is typical for this pack. Second source: InsideEVs (2019 Niro EV, same pack) saw 25 kW at 80 %; Car and Driver Niro EV 10-90 % in 65 min, peak 74 kW.
